items.title: Beyond procedural technicalities: The scope of amendment under Order VI Rule 17 CPC
items.summary: Pleadings set out a case of the parties to the suit and determine the issues to be considered by the Court. During the course of the hearing of the suit, the parties may find it necessary to amend their pleadings to incorporate additional facts, clarify existing averments, or seek further relief. Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) empowers courts to permit amendments to pleadings if such amendments are necessary for determining the real questions in controversy between the parties. The said provision seeks to balance two important considerations, i.e., ensuring that a dispute is decided completely and avoiding belated amendments that may delay proceedings or cause prejudice to the opposite party. The Supreme Court’s decision in Haramani Sahoo and Others v. Lalita Nayak and Others reiterates these principles and explains how courts should approach amendment applications filed after commencement of trial. Statutory position under Order VI Rule 17 CPC Order VI Rule 17 of the CPC permits either party to alter or amend its pleadings at any stage of the proceedings, on such terms as may be just, where the amendment is necessary for determining the real questions
